newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor proposes $32.9 bln preliminary budget.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor proposes $32.9 bln preliminary budget.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani on Thursday proposed a $32.9 billion preliminary budget for fiscal 1998 that includes $250 million of tax cuts, mainly to end the city's tax on clothing that costs over $500.
The preliminary plan also sets how the Guiliani Administration would close a projected $1.4 billion budget gap.
The gap closing program includes $558 million of savings at city agencies, asset sales of $125 million, additional state aid of $210 million, and $415 million of savings on entitlement programs.
Further, part of an expected surplus from fiscal 1997 would be used to prepay $391 million of debt service for fiscal 1998.

The Board of Education, which has seen its share of the city's budget fall sharply, would get a $500 million boost in the fiscal years 1997-1999, enabling it to create 64,000 new seats for New York City's overcrowded schools.

The mayor's preliminary plan included an outline of capital spending for the next 10 years, which would total $43.4 billion, and be partly funded with $23.4 billion of general obligation bonds. The rest of the funds would come from the state and federal governments.

A new finance authority that the Giuliani Administration has proposed as way to sidestep its debt cap would sell $7.5 billion of bonds over the period. Albany lawmakers have yet to approve the plan. Further, the city Water Finance Authority would sell $8 billion of bonds over the next 10 years under the mayor's plan, which also called for the state Dormitory Authority to issue $2.1 billion of bonds for the city.
The state would also have to approve Giuliani's plan for the city to eliminate its four percent tax on clothing that costs less than $500.
